title: Active Teacher Selection for Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a core limitation in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF): most systems assume feedback comes from a single human teacher, even though real feedback often comes from multiple teachers with different levels of expertise, rationality, and cost. The authors argue that this assumption can make reward learning less accurate and potentially less safe or reliable.

To study this, they introduce the Hidden Utility Bandit (HUB) framework, which models learning from multiple teachers whose feedback quality and cost differ. They also propose Active Teacher Selection (ATS), an algorithm that decides both when to query teachers and which teacher to query, using a POMDP formulation solved with POMCPOW and custom rollouts. The paper presents theoretical derivations, query-complexity bounds, and simulations, rather than a human-subject educational intervention.

The empirical evaluation uses two non-education domains: a paper-recommendation task and a COVID-19 vaccine-testing proof of concept. In both settings, ATS outperforms baseline methods by learning more accurate hidden utilities while using teacher queries more efficiently. The main conclusion is that explicitly modeling teacher heterogeneity and actively choosing teachers can improve reward learning robustness, accuracy, and efficiency. The paper does not study teachers, students, schools, or classroom implementation in an education context.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a theoretical/computational methods paper with simulation and proof-of-concept applications, not a study of an educational intervention or a causal evaluation in schools. It does not provide an empirical design relevant to K-12 evidence criteria.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct educational outcome or student impact is measured. The paper proposes infrastructure for safer multi-teacher reward learning and demonstrates algorithmic performance in non-educational domains, so educational impact is indirect and unquantified.

interventions.use_case: Framework and algorithm for active teacher selection in reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF), modeling multiple teachers with different rationality/expertise/costs and choosing when and which teacher to query.
